extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and house-style rules for creating, naming, structuring, and formatting pages on ProofWiki, including LaTeX, linking, sourcing, and linguistic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to house style
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors should feel welcome to contribute, but over time are expected to master and adhere to house style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Help:House Style for details; minor edits may be applied to submissions to match house style. If unsure, raise questions at Help:Questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check before creating a page
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for the page name first; if it exists do not recreate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a page via the search 'Create the page "Proof name"' link, via a red link, or by entering a direct URL; if you land on 'There is currently no text in this page...' click 'create this page' to edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page creation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages may be created by searching, following a red link, or entering a direct URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given (search result 'Create the page', clicking red link, direct URL like http://www.proofwiki.org/wiki/Riemann Hypothesis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not delete pages casually
rubrics_metrics.description: Page deletion is discouraged and restricted to trusted users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a page should be deleted, add {{Delete}} to the top of the page rather than deleting manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page title importance
rubrics_metrics.description: A good page title improves searchability, gives first impression, is used in links, and avoids name conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose descriptive titles to make it clear what the page contains before clicking links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific (page naming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Page names should be specific; single-word names should generally be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'Definition:Prime Ideal of Ring' over 'Definition:Prime Ideal'; include at least one noun; examples given for theorems and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundant words in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles should not start with articles such as 'A' or 'The' and should avoid unnecessary prefixes like 'Proof of ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Pythagorean Theorem', not 'The Pythagorean Theorem'; avoid making names artificially long unless needed for disambiguation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive titles for theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem titles should describe content accurately so a reader can guess what the theorem is about without visiting the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a theorem is an equivalence proof, make this clear by using 'iff' in the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't blindly trust literature for names
rubrics_metrics.description: Books may use simplified terminology; in ProofWiki use unambiguous, specific names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one name is standard but ambiguous, prefer a more specific title; prefer the name of the theorem only if no ambiguity exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Namespaces (naming conventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use page-type prefixes such as 'Definition:', 'Symbol:', 'Axiom:' to name and categorize pages appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After creating, add the page to the appropriate category (e.g., Category:Definitions). See Help:Categories for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rules for titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Page titles are case-sensitive and major words should be capitalized; certain small words should be lowercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowercase prepositions, pronouns, conjunctions (and, of, in, etc.) and certain short verbs (is, are, has, etc.). Variables in formulas generally not capitalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names containing formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for page names that include mathematical statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put no spaces between numbers added/subtracted/multiplied (use (1+2)x3); put spaces around equality/inequality and use '!=' for inequality; do not use LaTeX commands in page names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pages named after mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem/definition pages named for a mathematician should invoke the Namedfor / NamedforDef templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use {{Namedfor}} or {{NamedforDef}} to automatically place the page in corresponding categories; examples given and template usage demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple names for the same concept
rubrics_metrics.description: When a concept has several names, choose the preferred one (often the one named for a mathematician) unless obscure; set up redirects otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prefer Definition:Chebyshev Distance over Definition:Maximum Metric; create redirects and use Also known as / Also defined as sections as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed characters in page names
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain characters must not be used in page names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use: # < > [ ] | { } * & $ @ ; handle accented characters by using the exact name but create redirects for search convenience (see Help:Redirects#Accented characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: General page structure / format
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages generally follow the template: Theorem, Proof, Also see, Sources, [[Category:...]] with type 2 headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example layout provided. Sections should use type-2 headings and appear in a prescribed order; see House Style for section ordering rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required section order and capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections should be placed in the following order with exact capitalization: Definition / Theorem, Proof(s), Also defined as, Examples, Also known as, Also see, Named for, Historical Note, Linguistic Note, Technical Note, Sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other optional sections (Lemma, Corollary, Outline of Proof) are allowed; each should be a type-2 header; spacing conventions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of Definitions and Theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions/Theorems split into 'Let' lines introducing names and then, after two blank lines, the statement; the defined concept is displayed in bold throughout the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blank lines to separate the introductory 'Let' material and the actual statement; boldface the concept with three apostrophes to make it stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for house style, rigour is the only real prerequisite for proofs; separate different stages with subsections or whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want others to check your proof, add the {{Proofread}} template. Break complex proofs into labeled subsections or blocks for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid general 'Notes' sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not create a general 'Notes' section; instead, place remarks into one of the prescribed sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If remarks belong to a specific type (historical, linguistic, technical), use the corresponding named section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Also defined as / Also known as guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Also defined as' when a single name has multiple definitions (typically within same field); use 'Also known as' when a concept has multiple common names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a synthesis between these sections; all alternative names should appear in bold; draw attention to name collisions with links and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Also see section usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Also see' should contain bulleted list of closely related internal links; definitions should be referenced directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bullet points (asterisk). Example: * [[Definition:Increasing Sequence of Sets]]; reference associated categories using {{Link-to-category}} where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of name and Namedfor template
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Source of Name' section is created by the {{Namedfor}} template and should list the mathematician(s) the page is named for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use {{Namedfor|Name|cat=Surname}} and include multiple names via name2/cat2 parameters when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Note usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Historical Note' to elaborate interesting history; if brief, consider placing it after {{Namedfor}} invocation; if large, transclude a separate page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider creating a structured category for history if substantial historical content is expected; transclusion recommended for long material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic Note usage
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-common natural-language terms, provide pronunciation, plural form, and etymology where appropriate; boldface words relating to the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronunciation in simple phonetic English with syllable hyphenation and italics for stress. Document UK/US spelling differences in this section when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Note usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain involved LaTeX rendering or notation tricks in a 'Technical Note' section when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples and code for rendering notation; link to Definition:Convergence in Measure for an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add a Sources section
rubrics_metrics.description: Every page should include a Sources section listing sources backing the page; it's of paramount importance for reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Help:Sources for detailed rules; list multiple sources first in chronological order then alphabetically by first author's surname; in citations prefer chapter/section identifiers rather than page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories at bottom
rubrics_metrics.description: Add appropriate categories at the bottom of the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Help:Categories for documentation on how to choose and add categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text styles (wiki markup)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use three single quotes for bold, two for italic, five for bold+italic, and ... for fixed-width text; avoid tag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '''Bold text''' → Bold text. Use <code> to avoid rendering issues with MediaWiki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line breaking and sentence-per-line
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking lines in the editor does not force line breaks in output; place each sentence on its own line and use blank lines to force paragraph breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To force a line break in output, separate with a single blank line. Maintain one-sentence-per-line discipline for readability and diffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section and subsection markup & spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use equals signs for section headings (== Section ==) and follow spacing conventions: two blank lines before a heading and one blank line after; each sentence on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsections use '===' etc.; see Help:House Style for accepted house style regarding sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indenting and bullet points
rubrics_metrics.description: Indent with a colon ':'; displayed equations must be preceded by a single colon per house style; bullet lists use '*' with no empty-line spacing between successive items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple colons for larger indents. Note the empty-line guideline is relaxed for successive list items to avoid spacing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal linking syntax and best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Link internal pages with [[Page Name]]; change link text using pipe '[[Page Name|display text]]'; link to sections with '#'; prefer transclusion for section reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: [[Pythagoras's Theorem|here]] or [[Pythagoras's Theorem#The Classic Proof|here]]. On ProofWiki prefer linking to subpages (transclusion) for canonical references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redirects for synonyms
rubrics_metrics.description: If a theorem/definition has multiple common names, create one primary page and redirect secondary names to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create redirects with the code '#Redirect [[Page Name]]' rather than creating separate duplicate pages; see Help:Redirects for house style.

rubrics_metrics.name: External linking syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: External links use single square brackets with URL and optional label: [http://example.com Label].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: [http://www.google.com Google] → Google.

rubrics_metrics.name: References with <ref> and <references/>
rubrics_metrics.description: Create inline references using <ref>...</ref> and list them with <references/> near the end of the article, typically under a 'References' header placed above 'Sources'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage provided; prefer collecting references under 'References' section directly above 'Sources'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transclusion feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MediaWiki transclusion to display part of a page verbatim on another page when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transclusion is involved; see Help:Transclusion for full documentation and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProofWiki extension notice
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofWiki uses a site-specific extension (Pr∞fWiki extension) adding constructs not in base MediaWiki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Help:ProofWiki Extension for documentation on site-specific features and templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume LaTeX familiarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors are expected to be familiar with some form of LaTeX; MathJax is used for rendering on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unfamiliar, a web search or the external references can help; MathJax differs subtly from MediaWiki math syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX inline delimiter preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use single dollar signs $ ... $ for inline math; \( ... \) also works but is less recommended; avoid old <math>...</math> usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find <math> tags on transcluded pages, change them to $ signs; <math> may not convert properly on transcluded pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace unsupported LaTeX commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain older LaTeX macros are unsupported by MathJax and should be replaced with standard commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: replace '\or' with '\lor', '\and' with '\land', '\reals' with '\R', '\exist' with '\exists', and '\texttt' with '\mathtt'. Add more replacements to the list as encountered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting new LaTeX commands
rubrics_metrics.description: New LaTeX commands can be requested and discussed on Symbols:LaTeX Commands/ProofWiki Specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the desired command and example usage; many site-specific macros are transcluded in documentation on that page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aligned equations and display conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Displayed equations should be preceded by a single colon per house style and aligned material has special considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colons for indentation of displayed equations; see LaTeX Code Style and Aligned Material sections for known issues and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical symbol usage and typography
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on symbol sets, inline vs displayed equations, big operators, fonts, logical symbols, punctuation niceties, and Q.E.D. conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the site symbol set and punctuation niceties (e.g., Roman \d for derivatives). See the 'Mathematical Symbols' section for detailed rules on many symbol usages (d of calculus, fonts, big operators, Q.E.D.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic style: language and sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear English exposition; prefer terse forms but prioritize clarity; each sentence should be short and on its own line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid filler words where possible but keep clarity and completeness. For definitions prefer concise 'X is ...' wording rather than elaborate phrases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid parenthetical notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inserting extended explanations in parentheses inside sentences; this clashes with short-sentence house style and causes confusion with mathematical notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead place clarifying remarks in separate sentences or appropriate sections; examples show how parenthetical notation can confuse readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize filler words
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce filler phrases ('it follows that', 'we have', etc.) unless they improve clarity or completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer terse citation style like 'From X:' instead of verbose lead-ins. Clarity overrides terseness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: prefer simple 'is' phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: In definitions use direct phrasing such as 'X is ...' rather than 'X is called...', 'X is known as...', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep definitions concise and avoid unnecessary linguistic constructs that add verbosity without information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid empty statements and waffle
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include statements that impart no information (e.g., 'The first part is easy', 'This is trivial').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use templates like {{handwaving}} and {{explain}} where appropriate; do not pad pages with filler content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization in sentence continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a sentence starts with a displayed mathematical expression and continues with a 'where' clause, do not capitalize the continuation as a new sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formatting shows 'Let: ... where ...' rather than capitalizing 'Where' after a displayed expression; maintain sentence continuity across lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering and formatting of Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: List multiple sources first in chronological order and then alphabetically by first author's surname; prefer chapter/section identifiers over page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided (Definition:Set Union) showing BookReference usage with section markers like '§ 4'. Avoid page numbers because reprints alter pagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable online sources (limited list)
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofWiki explicitly accepts a limited set of online resources as general citation sources (MathWorld, PlanetMath, MacTutor, Khan Academy, Metamath, Mizar, OEIS, SpringerOnline, StackExchange under constraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these web resources are generally acceptable; StackExchange links are highly restricted: only link to an answer (not a question) and only in exceptional circumstances (OP exhausted other options or result only found on SE answer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable online sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use certain online materials as sources because they are unstable or unreliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not generally acceptable: university lecture notes available online, links to homework help forums, discussion pages in any web forum, and Wikipedia (prefer primary sources instead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting sources when splitting content
rubrics_metrics.description: If you split a referenced theorem/proof/definition into multiple pages, update and reference the source at every resulting page and update process flow ordering according to the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use per-page referencing and maintain the order in which elements appear in the original source when splitting content across pages.
